agency: City of Atlanta Department of City Planning, Office of Buildings

code_edition.value: 2023 National Electrical Code with no Georgia amendments (statewide mandatory minimum code)
code_edition.quote: New Mandatory Code and Amendment Effective January 1, 2025: 2023 National Electrical Code with no amendments.

who_may_file.conditions: Contractors Exception and Contractors Affidavit forms are listed on the Applications, Forms, and Checklists page, but the PDFs could not be opened directly to verify homeowner electrical permit eligibility
who_may_file.quote: Contractor (Reference Material) * A2L REFRIGERANT PRESSURE TEST AFFIDAVIT. * Contractors Exception. * Contractors Affidavit. * Agent Affidavit Authorization.

requirements.item: Apply for new/upgraded service via Builders Line with phase, voltage, load, and solar/generator details
requirements.quote: When contacting the Company regarding new service, be prepared to provide all information related to phase requirements, voltage, loading, etc., including any information on specific requirements. ( i.e., solar (PV) or generator)

requirements.item: Service entrance and meter socket must meet Georgia Power Blue Book and pass city/county inspection before connection
requirements.quote: An inspector from the constituted authority (e.g. city or county) inspects all wiring and equipment prior to us connecting service. We set the meter and the job is done!

requirements.item: Submit residential solar/battery interconnection application via PowerClerk with one-line drawing and panel, inverter, and battery specs
requirements.quote: Facility and technical information, including a one-line drawing and panel and inverter specifications. If battery storage is included, battery specifications must also be provided.

requirements.item: Pass county/city inspection, sign Interconnection Agreement, complete witness test/meter reprogramming, and receive Permission to Operate
requirements.quote: Once all steps have been successfully completed, the customer will receive an email from Georgia Power granting permission to turn their system on and begin generating.

open_questions: The PDFs linked on https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/city-planning/zoning-development-permitting-services/applications-forms-and-checklists—including 'EV Charger Affidavit Form', 'Electrical Permit Application', 'Description of Electrical Permits & Inspections', 'Contractors Exception', 'Submittal Info-Solar Roof Install - Res', 'Submittal Info-Solar Roof Install - Express', and 'PV - Inspection Checklist'—could not be opened directly to verify their verbatim contents, revision dates, homeowner electrical permit eligibility, or battery energy storage system (ESS) rules.

Georgia Department of Community Affairs announced 2026 Georgia Amendments to the 2023 National Electrical Code effective January 1, 2027 (https://dca.georgia.gov/announcement/2025-12-09/new-codes-jan-2027); as of 2026-11-24, the 2023 NEC with no Georgia amendments remains in effect.

No City of Atlanta-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet, mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83 vs. 220.87), EV charger service load factor, or minimum plan sheet size was found on atlantaga.gov.
